claims.text: Short-range chemical ordering produces local lattice distortions in a single-phase Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti high-entropy alloy.
The local lattice distortions directly modulate electron-phonon coupling.
Short-range-order-induced modulation of electron-phonon coupling governs Tc in Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti.
Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti can form a chemically homogeneous, single-phase bcc superconducting alloy.
The proposed as-cast Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti starting material has minimal short-range order.
XRD and EDS can verify the single-phase bcc structure and chemical homogeneity of the starting alloy.
Systematic heat treatment can produce different degrees or types of short-range chemical order without changing overall composition.
Short-range order locally distorts the bcc lattice framework.
Increasing local chemical order intensifies electron-phonon coupling by altering phonon modes and increasing scattering.
The proposed increase in electron-phonon coupling raises Tc and changes or increases the superconducting gap.
Samples with greater short-range order will have Tc values elevated by a few kelvins and altered gap structure relative to minimally ordered samples.
An as-cast or rapidly solidified Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti specimen provides a minimally ordered baseline.
NbTi has a sufficiently similar crystal structure and nominal electron-phonon coupling to serve as a reference.
Second-phase precipitation, compositional segregation, and magnetic impurities would confound the proposed relationship between short-range order and superconductivity.
Subtle composition differences, thermal history, strain, point defects, and measurement technique may affect the measured Tc shift.
A failure to observe any consistent change in Tc or gap properties as short-range order varies would falsify the proposed governing role of short-range order.
